newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain presses EU to ease beef export ban.
newsitem.headline: Britain presses EU to ease beef export ban.

text.p: Britain on Monday pressed its EU partners to take a first step in easing a worldwide ban on British beef exports, saying it had fulfilled the pre-conditions agreed at the June 1995 Florence summit, British officials said.

The ban was imposed a year ago after the British government triggered a massive public health scare by admitting that the brain wasting disease bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) could be transmitted to humans who ate infected beef.

The message was delivered by Lord Lindsay, representing the British government after agriculture minister Douglas Hogg left an EU farm ministers' meeting early to fly back to London for an important parliamentary vote.
In February, Britain proposed that exports of cattle from Northern Irish and other herds certified to be free of the disease should be exempted.

But a European Commission spokesman appeared to rule out any early easing of the ban, saying that more veterinary inspections were needed to check whether Britain had complied with the terms of the Florence agreement.
The British proposal would also have to be studied by various EU veterinary committees, he added.
